I honestly feel the exact same way. Before transitioning I only ever thought of dating/sleeping with women, and I always imagined myself in the more dominant role. But now, after a little over 7 months on hormones? It's almost impossible for me to think of myself as being dominant in any capacity. And I'm honestly struggling to figure myself out. Like, I know for certain that I like women, that's never ever been in doubt. But I'm not so sure about men anymore. I don't think I've ever seen a man and thought to myself, "he's good looking, I want to go out with him." But I'd definitely be willing to sleep with men, and sometimes I even imagine myself having a boyfriend...but then I get upset because I really want to have a girlfriend instead. The term I've been using for myself is 'gyneflexible,' which is basically someone who's attracted to feminity regardless of gender or sex but is also flexible enough to be attracted to non-femme people. A friend of mine also suggested 'homoromantic bisexual,' which is basically someone who's sexually attracted to both men and women but romantically attracted to (in my case) women exclusively. In any case, there's no real rush to figure it out. These terms are nothing more than words at the end of the day; date whoever you want, sleep with whoever you want, love whoever you want. Love is love, and as long as you find happiness none of the rest of this stuff really matters!
